etymologies.etymologyHTML: From active +‎ -ist.

definitions.definition: One who is politically active in the role of a citizen; especially, one who campaigns for change.

quote.citation: 2013 August 10, “Can China clean up fast enough?”, in The Economist, volume 408, number 8848:
quote.text: It has jailed environmental activists and is planning to limit the power of judicial oversight by handing a state-approved body a monopoly over bringing environmental lawsuits.

quote.citation: 2023 January 11, “Network News: Court decision overturned: Six HS2 activists face retrial”, in RAIL, number 974, page 9:
quote.text: The six activists will now face a retrial at Highbury Magistrates' Court, in front of a new judge.

definitions.definition: One who is conspicuously active in carrying out any occupational or professional functions.

quote.citation: 1971 September 26, “They Will Affect The Nation For Years To Come”, in New York Times:
quote.text: Even in the area of free speech, Justice Harlan sometimes emerged as more activist than his brother

quote.citation: 2009 December 10, “Angst Over GM's Activist Board”, in BusinessWeek:
quote.text: Now GM has what may well be the most activist board ever.

quote.citation: 2012 June 1, “Gov. Christie's court pick blocked”, in Cherry Hill Courier Post (NJ):
quote.text: Gov. Chris Christie has long complained that New Jersey's Supreme Court is too liberal and too activist
